tests_added: The pure post-game state machine retains uploading and does not consume settled samples before handoff_confirmed, then completes only after three distinct new settled samples.
The pure state machine keeps a local/index mutation with no caught upload evidence pending before handoff and permits completion only after the post-handoff quorum.
SyncthingMonitor fake timers prove a buffered upload survives three pre-handoff settled samples, returns uploading at handoff, and reaches COMPLETE only after three later samples.
The exit lifecycle decision publishes syncthing_uploading for a buffered-upload handoff result.
A watched-folder sequence advance produces uploading even when the same relevant peer emits only a FolderCompletion event for another folder; that unscoped completion is absent from peer_completions.
design_decisions: Peer completion is post-game-only. A FolderCompletion is accepted only when its folder and configured remote device both match the resolved backup folder; the backend begins with a REST baseline for each currently connected relevant peer.

A watched-folder local-index mutation requires fresh peer observations made after that mutation. Event ordering and monotonic observation time establish freshness; FolderCompletion.sequence is remote-device state and is never compared to the Deck's local sequence.

Incomplete peer evidence and watched-folder mutation hold uploading for 2.5 seconds so an index update and terminal completion in one event batch remain visible to the 500 ms frontend poller. RemoteDownloadProgress remains supplemental evidence, not the acknowledgement source.

Post-game COMPLETE requires local settlement plus no outstanding need from every peer that remains connected and relevant. Disconnected/offline configured peers are intentionally outside this confirmation, while pre-game settlement remains local/incoming and never queries peer completion.
Diagnostics aggregate only peer counts and needed bytes/items/deletes. Device IDs, peer percentages, and raw responses remain backend-only and never enter logs or RPC payloads.
The reducer gates only post-game settled-sample counting on handoffActivated. Pre-game settlement and all existing transfer classification remain unchanged.

Pre-handoff samples reset the post-game settle counter instead of carrying it into the handoff, so the existing three-sample stability check is a visible post-handoff dwell rather than already-consumed history.

Task 2 changed test_watch_ignores_other_folder_traffic_shared_with_relevant_peer from watched-folder status sequences 6, 7 to 5, 5, and Review 02 required this rationale. The original sequences now correctly arm post-game outbound evidence because they advance the watched folder's local index; keeping them flat preserves that test's actual assertion that unrelated-folder traffic alone remains idle. The companion regression restores the missing combination and proves uploading comes from the watched-folder mutation, not the peer's unrelated FolderCompletion.
